sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Wanib Sign Language' (stub; cites Reed & Rumsey 2020 p. 150 via Google Books X0fODwAAQBAJ, and an ELAR sample)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Two sentences: reported sign language, possibly a village sign language, in a Heyo-speaking community just west of Mehek SL; 'Wanib SL follows the SVO word order of Heyo, whereas Mehek SL follows the SOV word order of Mehek'.

sources.citation: Reed, Lauren W. 2019. Sign Languages of Western Highlands, Papua New Guinea, and their Challenges for Sign Language Typology. MA thesis, Australian National University (open, hdl:1885/165444)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Wanib: a full-text search for stress/accent Wanib/Heyo/Diaz/Sandaun/Torricelli = 0 hits; only Sepik mention (p. 97) is an unnamed 2018 video of two deaf men in a Sepik village. For the Western Highlands SLs it says (p. 62) the signing 'does not exhibit phonological contrast below the level of the word'; no stress/prominence statement for any PNG sign language.

sources.citation: ELAR collection 0550, Thomas Diaz (University at Buffalo), 'Documentation of Heyo [auk], a Torricelli language of Papua New Guinea', 2018-2020, hdl:2196/00-0000-0000-0012-57CA-D; item 'Some words and phrases in Wanib Sign Language' (listing page 8)
sources.note: Nothing. The item is a recording (access level U_UserAccess = ELAR login required), listed among Heyo narrative items with no description shown; it is the only primary material on Wanib SL. Not a written description.
